title: Information nudging, attitude, and protective behaviours against Nipah virus in India, 2026: a national experimental survey
abstract: Background: Nipah virus (NiV) poses a significant public health threat due to its high fatality, yet public readiness for medical countermeasures remains understudied. We aimed to evaluate the associations of perceived severity and benefits information nudges with the dimensions of the Health Belief Model (HBM), identify highly responsive populations, and assess whether changes in HBM dimensions mediate the associations between information nudges and protective behavioural intentions in India. Methods: We conducted a nationwide experimental web survey among Indian adults between 6 and 18 February 2026. The survey contained an embedded information nudge module in which participants were randomly assigned to one of three groups: a perceived severity nudge, a perceived benefits nudge, or no nudge. We assessed changes in HBM dimensions using analysis of covariance. Six predictive models were evaluated to identify subpopulations highly susceptible to cognitive shifts. Mediation analyses were performed to estimate the indirect effects of nudges on intentions to promptly seek medical care, receive vaccination, and accept treatment. Results: Our sample comprised 1,124 participants randomly assigned to receive a perceived severity nudge (n = 373), a perceived benefits nudge (n = 376), or no nudge (n = 375). Compared with no nudge, the severity nudge significantly increased perceived severity (adjusted mean difference (AMD) = 0.17; 95% confidence interval (CI) = 0.05, 0.30; P = 0.005) and cues to action (AMD = 0.20; 95% CI = 0.09, 0.32; P < 0.001), while the benefits nudge significantly increased cues to action (0.30; 95% CI = 0.19, 0.41; P < 0.001). Predictive modelling (extreme gradient boosting: area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) = 0.717; logistic regression: AUROC = 0.789) identified baseline health beliefs and residence outside prior outbreak regions as dominant contributors to nudge responsiveness. Mediation analyses indicated significant indirect effects of the severity nudge on treatment intention via perceived severity (effect estimate (β) = 0.016; 95% CI = 0.002, 0.032), as well as the perceived benefits nudge via cues to action on both vaccination intention (β = 0.024; 95% CI = 0.001, 0.054) and treatment intention (β = 0.028; 95% CI = 0.002, 0.055). Neither information nudge significantly influenced promptly seeking medical care. Conclusions: Targeted information nudges could alter health beliefs and influence vaccination and treatment readiness through distinct psychological pathways.

title: Development of a Pan-Proteome Multi-Epitope Vaccine Candidate Against Nipah Virus Using Reverse Vaccinology and Immunoinformatics Approaches
abstract: Nipah virus (NiV) is a high-consequence zoonotic pathogen for which no licensed human vaccine is currently available. This study applied a consensus-guided pan-proteome immunoinformatics framework to design and prioritize a multi-epitope vaccine candidate using sequence information from all nine NiV proteins. A total of 901 NiV protein sequences were retrieved, of which 842 passed quality filtering and were processed through clustering, multiple-sequence alignment, and protein-specific consensus generation. Consensus-derived fragments were screened for cytotoxic T-lymphocyte, helper T-lymphocyte, and B-cell epitopes, followed by multi-criterion filtering based on antigenicity, allergenicity, toxicity, conservancy, class-specific immune-response properties, and human-proteome similarity. Ten epitope-selection strategies were combined with two adjuvant candidates and three construct architectures to generate 60 vaccine constructs. Shortlisted candidates were subsequently evaluated for physicochemical properties, HLA population coverage, structural characteristics, conformational B-cell epitopes, TLR3 docking, molecular dynamics, immune-response simulation, and expression-oriented optimization. VC033_V6_BD_L03 construct was prioritized as the lead candidate and showed combined predicted population coverage of 99.78% worldwide and 99.96% in South Asia. Docking against human TLR3 structure 1ZIW yielded a ClusPro score of -1624.8. During a 100-ns molecular-dynamics simulation, the complex underwent early conformational reorganization followed by lower late-phase structural variation and persistent interchain hydrogen bonding. MM/GBSA analysis yielded a mean interaction-energy estimate of -20.52, 15.42 kcal/mol. C-ImmSim predicted coordinated humoral and cellular responses, while codon optimization generated a 1,539-bp expression sequence compatible with virtual cloning into pET-28a(+). These analyses prioritize VC033_V6_BD_L03 as a consensus-derived, pan-proteome NiV multi-epitope vaccine candidate for experimental evaluation of expression, immunogenicity, safety, and protective efficacy.

title_zh: 使用反向疫苗学和免疫信息学方法开发针对 尼帕病毒 的泛蛋白质组多表位 疫苗 候选药物

This study applied a consensus-guided pan-proteome immunoinformatics framework to design and prioritize a multi-epitope vaccine candidate using sequence information from all nine NiV proteins. A total of 901 NiV protein sequences were retrieved, of which 842 passed quality filtering and were processed through clustering, multiple-sequence alignment, and protein-specific consensus generation. Consensus-derived fragments were screened for cytotoxic T-lymphocyte, helper T-lymphocyte, and B-cell epitopes, followed by multi-criterion filtering based on antigenicity, allergenicity, toxicity, conservancy, class-specific immune-response properties, and human-proteome similarity. Ten epitope-selection strategies were combined with two adjuvant candidates and three construct architectures to generate 60 vaccine constructs. Shortlisted candidates were subsequently evaluated for physicochemical properties, HLA population coverage, structural characteristics, conformational B-cell epitopes, TLR3 docking, molecular dynamics, immune-response simulation, and expression-oriented optimization. VC033_V6_BD_L03 construct was prioritized as the lead candidate and showed combined predicted population coverage of 99.78% worldwide and 99.96% in South Asia. Docking against human TLR3 structure 1ZIW yielded a ClusPro score of -1624.8. During a 100-ns molecular-dynamics simulation, the complex underwent early conformational reorganization followed by lower late-phase structural variation and persistent interchain hydrogen bonding. MM/GBSA analysis yielded a mean interaction-energy estimate of -20.52, 15.42 kcal/mol. C-ImmSim predicted coordinated humoral and cellular responses, while codon optimization generated a 1,539-bp expression sequence compatible with virtual cloning into pET-28a(+). These analyses prioritize VC033_V6_BD_L03 as a consensus-derived, pan-proteome NiV multi-epitope vaccine candidate for experimental evaluation of expression, immunogenicity, safety, and protective efficacy.

title: Stakeholder-informed use cases and target product characteristics for vaccines and therapeutics for Nipah virus disease
abstract: Nipah virus (NiV) is a deadly zoonotic pathogen with potential for severe outbreaks. We convened a multi-stakeholder expert consultation to define potential implementation strategies and use cases for NiV countermeasures across hypothetical outbreak scenarios and conditions. Participants identified distinct roles for vaccines, monoclonal antibodies (mAbs), and small-molecule therapeutics (SMTs) for prevention, post-exposure protection, and treatment. These stakeholder-informed outputs are intended to inform product development, target product profiles, and equitable access during future outbreaks.
authors: On behalf of the Nipah Countermeasure Use Case Working Group

title: Observation of Nipah Virus Evolution Using the ATG Genomic Walks
abstract: In this paper, 32 complete genomic sequences of human-origin Nipah viruses registered in GenBank® from 1999 to 2025 are analyzed by tracking distributions of ATG triplets. The trajectories of these triplets are constructed, and their divergence parameter is calculated, revealing an increased value typical of highly mutated viruses that can form separate families with distinct properties. This conclusion aligns with the large deviation observed in the fractal dimension parameters of the distribution of inter-ATG-triplet distances in genomic sequences. The simulation results are compared with earlier data for SARS-CoV-2, MERS-CoV, dengue, and Ebola viruses.

title: Immunogenicity of an Fc-Fused Nipah Virus Attachment Glycoprotein Vaccine Candidate
abstract: Nipah virus (NiV) comprises two major genotypes, the Malaysia (NiV-M) and Bangladesh (NiV-B) strains. It is a zoonotic pathogen with high virulence in humans and pigs. The attachment glycoprotein (G) is considered a target for NiV vaccine development. Here, we report an Fc-G fusion protein, generated by fusing the ectodomain of NiV-B G to an immunoglobulin G1 (IgG1) fragment crystallizable (Fc), and evaluated its immunogenicity in three animal species. In mice, Fc-G was evaluated together with an unfused G comparator and induced potent G-specific antibody levels and strong neutralizing activity against NiV pseudovirus. Robust antibody responses were elicited in Fc-G-immunized Syrian hamsters and pigs; high-level neutralizing antibodies against both NiV-M and NiV-B were also detected. Neutralizing antibody titers remained high at 91 days post-immunization in hamsters. These findings demonstrate that Fc-G elicits robust, durable binding and cross-reactive neutralizing antibody responses.

These findings demonstrate that Fc-G elicits robust, durable binding and cross-reactive neutralizing antibody responses.

title: Identification and Fc-Formatting of Alpaca Single-Domain Antibodies Targeting the Nipah Virus Attachment Glycoprotein
abstract: Nipah virus (NiV) is a WHO priority pathogen with case-fatality rates of 40–75%, and no antiviral therapeutic is licensed for human use. The attachment glycoprotein (G) mediates receptor engagement and is a validated target for neutralizing antibodies. Here, we aimed to isolate alpaca-derived single-domain antibodies (VHHs) against the NiV G head domain. Two alpacas were immunized with a baculovirus-expressed, truncated NiV G ectodomain (residues 170–575); peripheral blood mononuclear cells from the higher-responding animal were used to build an immune phage display library of 3.2 × 108 transformants. Four rounds of biopanning enriched antigen-specific phages approximately 120-fold, and sequencing of 183 reactive clones yielded seven unique VHHs. All seven bound to recombinant NiV G, observed by ELISA, and inhibited entry of a VSV-based NiV pseudovirus. VHH-0G8 and VHH-1B6 were most active, with fitted IC50 values of 1.34 and 1.76 μg/mL (≈89 and 118 nM). Reformatting the two leads as human IgG1 Fc-YTE fusions lowered the fitted IC50 to 0.97 and 1.09 μg/mL (≈12 and 13 nM); because a wild-type Fc comparator was not included, this reflects the Fc-YTE format (M252Y/S254T/T256E, which enhances binding to FcRn to extend serum half-life) as a whole. A tandem 0G8/1B6 construct did not show a statistically significant improvement in neutralization compared to the Fc fusions (IC50 = 1.08 μg/mL, ≈36 nM). Computational docking placed the two VHHs on non-overlapping surfaces of the G head, raising the hypothesis that a tandem format could enhance neutralization; however, this synergy was not experimentally observed and requires further format optimization. These VHHs provide starting points for NiV antibody development and require authentic virus and in vivo evaluation.

title: Ontwikkeling van strategieën ter behandeling en preventie van henipavirusinfecties
abstract: Henipaviruses are negative-strand RNA viruses in the Paramyxoviridae family with currently five species: Cedar, Ghanaian bat, Hendra, Mojang and Nipah henipaviruses. They are naturally harbored by pteropid fruit bats (flying foxes) and microbats of several species found throughout the tropics and subtropics. Henipavirus outbreaks in humans have occurred in northern Australia and Southeast Asia since the mid-1990s. Hendra virus (HeV) has been reported nearly annually since 1994 in the eastern states of Australia, while Nipah virus (NiV) outbreaks in humans were first reported in 1998-99 in Malaysia and Singapore and are reported almost annually in India and Bangladesh. The broad geographical distribution of the henipavirus natural animal reservoir, the high overall NiV and HeV case fatality rate in humans as well as the growing evidence of multiple routes of virus transmission, including human-to-human transmission, are causes of serious concern for henipaviruses to become epidemic or pandemic, and have turned NiV and HeV viruses into high priority pathogens of the World Health Organization (WHO). Despite the recognized high epidemic and pandemic potential of henipaviruses, no safe and effective vaccines nor therapeutics are currently available for human use. This PhD project addresses this need and aims to discover novel small molecule antivirals directly acting against henipaviruses and preferably with pan-paramyxovirus activity. To this end, the PhD project has the following aims: 1. Set up and perform a high throughput phenotypic screening assay with Cedar virus (CedV), a non-pathogenic henipavirus that can serve as a surrogate for BSL-4 NiV/HeV. Confirm and validate henipavirus antiviral activity of hit compounds in multiple complementary assays. In addition, compounds will be assessed for activity against HeV and NiV by partner institutes and for broader-spectrum anti-paramyxovirus activity. In parallel, they will be used to isolate virus variants that show phenotypic resistance to the respective compounds in a first step to unravel their precise molecular mechanism of action. Establish the first CedV infection model in mice or hamster to allow future evaluation of the efficacy of small molecules in vivo.

abstract_zh: 亨尼帕病毒(亨尼帕病毒)是副粘病毒科(Paramyxoviridae)中的负链RNA病毒,目前包含五个物种: Cedar病毒、加纳果蝠病毒、亨德拉病毒、Mojang病毒和尼帕病毒。这些病毒的天然宿主是果蝠(pteropid 果蝠)和多种微蝙蝠,广泛分布于热带和亚热带地区。自1990年代中期以来,亨尼帕病毒在人类中已出现于澳大利亚北部和东南亚地区。亨德拉病毒(HeV)自1994年以来在澳大利亚东部各州几乎每年都有报告,而尼帕病毒(NiV)在人类中的首次报告则于1998-99年出现在马来西亚和新加坡,并且在印度和孟加拉国几乎每年都有报告。亨尼帕病毒在自然动物中的广泛地理分布、人类中高总体的尼帕病毒和亨德拉病毒死亡率,以及越来越多的证据表明病毒可通过多种途径传播,包括人传人传播,这些因素都引发了对亨尼帕病毒可能成为大流行或全球大流行的严重担忧,并使尼帕病毒和亨德拉病毒成为世界卫生组织(WHO)的高优先级病原体。尽管已认识到亨尼帕病毒具有高流行和大流行潜力,但目前尚无安全有效的抗病毒药物(疫苗)或治疗方法(传播)可供人类使用。本博士项目旨在满足这一需求,致力于发现直接作用于亨尼帕病毒的新小分子抗病毒药物(抗病毒药物),并优先考虑具有广谱抗副粘病毒活性的药物。为此,本博士项目的目标如下:1. 建立并执行一项针对Cedar病毒(CedV)的高通量表型筛选实验,CedV是一种非致病性的亨尼帕病毒,可作为BSL-4级别尼帕病毒/亨德拉病毒的替代物。确认并验证筛选中发现的化合物对亨尼帕病毒的活性,并在多种互补实验中进行验证。此外,这些化合物将由合作伙伴机构评估其对亨德拉病毒和尼帕病毒的活性,并评估其更广泛的抗副粘病毒活性。同时,这些化合物将用于分离表现出对相应化合物表型抗性的病毒变种,以初步揭示其精确的分子作用机制。建立小鼠或仓鼠中的首个CedV感染模型,以便未来评估小分子药物在体内的有效性。

title: Endothelial protein C receptor is an entry receptor for Langya virus
abstract: Langya virus (LayV) was recently discovered in infected individuals with febrile illness and classified as a Parahenipavirus, a group of poorly understood pathogens. LayV is distantly related to Nipah henipavirus which causes recurring outbreaks with case fatality rates reaching up to 90%. No vaccines or therapeutics are approved for use in humans for any parahenipavirus or henipavirus despite their broad geographic distribution and pandemic potential. Here, we discovered that human endothelial protein C receptor (EPCR) is an entry receptor for LayV and that the tetrameric LayV attachment glycoprotein (G) binds EPCR avidly. We reveal the molecular basis of LayV G recognition of the EPCR receptor and provide a blueprint of the determinants of receptor ortholog usage. We found that human and shrew EPCR orthologs promote cell entry of LayV and of the closely related Mojiang pseudoviruses. These results along with the detection of several Parahenipaviruses in shrews set these pathogens apart from Henipaviruses, which use Pteropid fruit bats as reservoir hosts. Our data support future surveillance efforts, by enabling prediction of EPCR utilization among newly discovered Parahenipaviruses, and the development and evaluation of countermeasures targeting this emerging group of human pathogens.

title: Deterministic–stochastic fractional-order modeling and optimal control of Nipah virus in hypertensive nephrosclerosis
abstract: Nipah virus is a zoonotic virus that causes severe respiratory and neurological disease and is spread through pigs, bats or contaminated food. This research develops a fractional-order mathematical model to investigate the co-infection dynamics of hypertensive nephrosclerosis and Nipah virus infection. The model is kept positive and bounded to guarantee biological reality, and the disease-free equilibrium E p l is studied. The basic reproduction number R 0 l p < 1 implies extinction of the infection while R 0 l p > 1 implies small outbreaks developing into epidemics. These results are backed up by bifurcation analysis, global stability analysis and existence and uniqueness proofs for the solution. Real Malaysian co-infection data was used to parameterise the model, and simulations were carried out for both deterministic and stochastic fractional systems. The fractional-order parameter has significant impact on the infection rates and convergence behaviour. The memory effects and nonlocal dynamics are described by using piecewise Caputo–Fabrizio derivatives. Stochastic perturbations are considered to model random environmental effects. The parameters were changed to highlight the role of vaccination and stochasticity in disease extinction. The amalgamation of Caputo–Fabrizio fractional calculus and stochastic modelling, supported by a novel numerical scheme, offers a robust and flexible approach to simulate co-infection dynamics under uncertainty. The framework is further validated by PRCC sensitivity analysis and MCMC parameter estimation. Optimal control strategies provide to control the co-infection spread with economic feasibility. To summarize, the model provides useful insights into the interaction between hypertensive nephrosclerosis and Nipah virus transmission, supporting the design of effective and economically feasible control strategies.

This research develops a fractional-order mathematical model to investigate the co-infection dynamics of hypertensive nephrosclerosis and Nipah virus infection. The memory effects and nonlocal dynamics are described by using piecewise Caputo–Fabrizio derivatives. Stochastic perturbations are considered to model random environmental effects. The parameters were changed to highlight the role of vaccination and stochasticity in disease extinction. The framework is further validated by PRCC sensitivity analysis and MCMC parameter estimation. Optimal control strategies provide to control the co-infection spread with economic feasibility. To summarize, the model provides useful insights into the interaction between hypertensive nephrosclerosis and Nipah virus transmission, supporting the design of effective and economically feasible control strategies.

abstract_zh: 尼帕病毒 是一种人畜共患病毒,会导致严重的呼吸道和神经系统疾病,并通过猪、蝙蝠或受污染的食物传播。本研究开发了一个分数阶数学模型来研究高血压肾硬化和 尼帕病毒 感染的共同感染动力学。模型保持正向且有界以保证生物学真实性,并研究无病平衡E p l。基本再生数R 0 l p < 1 意味着感染消失,而R 0 l p > 1 意味着小暴发 发展为流行病。这些结果得到分叉分析、全局稳定性分析以及解的存在性和唯一性证明的支持。真实的马来西亚双重感染数据用于参数化模型,并对确定性和随机分数系统进行了模拟。分数阶参数对感染率和收敛行为有显着影响。记忆效应和非局部动力学通过使用分段 Caputo-Fabrizio 导数来描述。随机扰动被认为是对随机环境影响进行建模。更改参数是为了突出 疫苗接种 和随机性在疾病灭绝中的作用。Caputo-Fabrizio 分数阶微积分和随机建模的融合,在新颖的数值方案的支持下,提供了一种稳健而灵活的方法来模拟不确定性下的共同感染动态。该框架通过 PRCC 敏感性分析和 MCMC 参数估计得到进一步验证。最佳控制策略可以以经济可行性来控制混合感染的传播。总而言之,该模型为高血压肾硬化与 尼帕病毒 传播 之间的相互作用提供了有用的见解,支持设计有效且经济可行的控制策略。
